items.title: 'Make it stop': 10 minutes of chaos in Lebanon's 'Black Wednesday'
items.description: The Israeli Defense Forces labelled it Operation Eternal Darkness. Inside Lebanon, it's now called Black Wednesday. ABC NEWS Verify has geolocated the explosions across 10 minutes of chaos.

items.title: Ben Roberts-Smith granted bail over alleged war crime murder offences
items.description: Ben Roberts-Smith is granted bail after spending a week in custody over alleged war crime offences.

items.title: Refinery blaze not cause to ratchet up fuel crisis response, Albanese says
items.description: Anthony Albanese has cut a trip to Malaysia short to visit Viva Energy Refinery in Geelong, which went up in flames late on Wednesday.

items.title: 'Six weeks of jet fuel' warning raises flight disruption fears in Europe
items.description: Europe could experience major flight disruptions within weeks as global energy officials warn the continent has "maybe six weeks of jet fuel left", which could lead to further price hikes and cancellations for Australian travellers.

items.title: Live: Trump says Iran war going 'swimmingly' as Lebanon says Israel violated ceasefire
items.description: Several hours into the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon, the Lebanese Army says "a number of violations" have occurred. Follow live.

items.title: Europe was a word British PMs dared not say. Then Donald Trump returned
items.description: Keir Starmer was never a fan of Brexit. Now, under the cover of the war in Iran and a fractured US relationship, he's looking to Europe to return Britain to the fold.

items.title: Mayor fears hidden cameras may have been in town hall change rooms for years
items.description: The Horsham mayor is worried that hidden cameras reportedly found in the town hall theatre change rooms could have been there for years.

items.title: Breaking: Missing votes counted in key SA seat see One Nation margin increase
items.description: One Nation has retained the South Australian seat of Narungga, following a count of ballots that were missed on election day.

items.title: Sydney childcare worker hit with 129 new child abuse charges
items.description: A Sydney childcare worker accused of using children to make abuse material has been charged with 129 new offences.

items.title: Mother of 11 who 'never thought we'd be homeless' pleads for help
items.description: Finding a home for a large family in a regional area has left one family camping on the side of the highway in rural New South Wales. Nationally, Indigenous people are over-represented in homelessness statistics.

items.title: Some Australians fear lockdowns. Economists say stagflation is the bigger risk
items.description: As fuel costs surge and supply fears grow, businesses and households say the economic shock from the war in the Middle East is already hitting home.

items.title: Harry and Meghan meet Bondi terror attack survivors on Sydney leg of tour
items.description: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex spoke with lifeguards who responded to the December 14 Bondi Beach terror attack and survivors.

items.title: Live: Oil spike risk, share market dive remains 'high'
items.description: The Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) expects Australian inflation to surge to 6 per cent, while adding another RBA interest rate hike to its forecast. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: St Kilda announces appeal against Collard ban for homophobic slur
items.description: St Kilda is appealing the nine-match ban given to Lance Collard for uttering a homophobic comment, saying the young forward maintains his innocence.

items.title: Why experts urge not to grow these popular invasive plants in your home
items.description: Agapanthus, morning glory or gazanias might be easy-growing plants in your home but their invasive nature can damage your garden and the environment. Here's what experts recommend.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: Trump's AI image, a 200m record and the Artemis II splashdown
items.description: It's Friday, and that means it's time to test your news knowledge from the past seven days. Were you paying attention this week?

items.title: How mobile phone cameras have helped unearth a mysterious kingdom
items.description: An exhibition bridges the gap between art and science by inviting visitors to imagine the world through the senses of other species and consider our own fragile relationship with nature.

items.title: What we know about the 'small fire' that became an 'unprecedented' Geelong refinery blaze
items.description: The "unprecedented" fire at one of the two remaining oil refineries in Australia took more than 12 hours to extinguish. Here's what we know about how it unfolded.

items.title: Australia is on the verge of aged care AI boom
items.description: Artificial intelligence-enabled robot companions, personal behaviour monitors and pain management apps could soon be used more widely within the sector.

items.title: Migration debate deserves less politicking from the Liberals
items.description: The Liberals need to resolve the internal ambiguities they have on big policy questions when it comes to migration.

items.title: Australian billionaire Andrew Forrest battles Meta over fake ads
items.description: Australian billionaire mining magnate Andrew Forrest is asking a US federal court in Silicon Valley to hold Meta accountable for scam ads using his likeness without permission.

items.title: Iranian footballers granted asylum in Australia 'overwhelmed' by support
items.description: Two Iranian footballers given refuge in Australia after the AFC Women's Asian Cup say they are focused on their health, safety and rebuilding their lives.

items.title: Elderly couple beg council to let them stay in Gold Coast caravan park
items.description: Time is running out for residents facing eviction from Kirra Beach Tourist Park. In 2018, the council told them they needed to move out by 2028 to make way for tourists, but with rising rent and property prices, they say they cannot afford to live anywhere else.

items.title: Former Arsenal, Juventus goalkeeper killed after car hit by train
items.description: Former Austria goalkeeper Alexander Manninger, who played for Arsenal and a string of Italian clubs, died on Thursday at the age of 48 after the car he was driving was hit by a train at a crossing near Salzburg.

items.title: By-election called one week after Qld state MP's death
items.description: Former Member for Stafford Jimmy Sullivan was found dead at his home earlier this month, after police were called to reports of a non-suspicious death.
